project_title: Draft and Send Demand Letter via Certified Mail and Email

project_metadata.job_title: Draft and Send Demand Letter via Certified Mail and Email
project_metadata.job_description: I am seeking a skilled professional to draft a demand letter on my behalf. The letter should be clear, concise, and legally sound, addressing all relevant points. After drafting, the letter must be sent via certified mail, and I would like to be included in the CC for the email version. This is a straightforward task, but attention to detail is vital to ensure the letter meets legal standards. If you have experience with legal documentation and communication, I would love to hear from you.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

I hope you’re doing well. Below is a concise overview.

In August 2023, Edwin Mason and John O’Brien signed a Secured Promissory Note for $1.23M, making themselves personally liable as borrowers. They also signed a Pledge & Security Agreement pledging their ownership interests in Meade Transportation, Inc. (MTI) and Virginia Freight Holdings, LLC (VFH). The Note had a 30% interest rate and matured after 90 days. Their failure to repay caused a default in November 2023 and activated the 35% default interest rate.

As of October 1, 2025, approximately $2.5M remains due, and default interest continues to accrue at more than $1,100 each day. Although repeated demands have been made, they have neither paid nor proposed an acceptable repayment plan. Instead, they have tried to introduce “updated loan agreements” that would diminish my secured position and eliminate their personal liability.

My request is straightforward:

Draft and issue a formal demand letter on your letterhead to Edwin Mason and John O’Brien that cites their duties under the Note and Security Agreement.

Mail the letter through U.S. Certified Mail so formal delivery is documented.

Afterward, email both Edwin and John with the demand letter attached, advise them of the certified mailing, and copy me.

To streamline the work, I have attached:

A chronology summary and balance calculation

A proposed demand letter for you to revise

A copy of the Secured Promissory Note

A copy of the Pledge & Security Agreement

I would like this finished within the next week. Because most of the drafting has already been completed, I would prefer a reasonable flat fee. My main objective is to have the demand formally issued on your letterhead so the record is established.

Please tell me when you are available to speak so we can agree on the flat fee.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Hi [CLIENT_NAME_001], I appreciate the highly detailed background—it was very useful. In my experience, collections remain extremely difficult even when the documentation is strong (note, guaranties, pledged equity): debtors delay, transfer assets, banks are nearly impossible to penetrate, and liens seldom produce cash. I do not handle forensic investigations or asset tracing. What I can provide is legal relief from New York, primarily a forceful demand that preserves the record. VA fraud complaints are another possible avenue, but they seldom produce results, and the Note’s VA arbitration provision restricts remedies pursued outside Virginia. For a flat fee, I can draft the demand letter, arrange certified mailing, and send it by email. I am also free to discuss this on Sunday.

There seem to be some unanticipated delays, creating concern that avoidance tactics may be involved, much like what happened when we sent the first demand letter, since this situation is quite unusual. Even so, we need to establish that we provided sufficient time for delivery before taking the next step. If anything, these seeming attempts at avoidance further support an argument of fraudulent and unlawful conduct.

With that in mind, my recommendation is to wait until Monday. By then, we can appropriately allege receipt of the initial demand letter and move ahead from a stronger position. The final decision is, of course, yours.

Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_002],

Because none of the addresses have provided any acknowledgment, even following the second demand letter, we now have four realistic options for the next step:

- Submit a UCC-1 lien to formally protect your position and create a public record of the debt against the company’s pledged assets.
- File a fraud complaint with the FBI or the local District Attorney based on the ongoing evasion and possible misrepresentation concerning the collateral.
- Engage a licensed research or skip-trace provider to verify the principals’ present locations and locate any assets that can be reached.
- Commence a civil lawsuit \(in either D.C. or Virginia\) to secure a judgment and pursue enforcement through receivership or asset seizure. Separately, I have now completed the original demand as well as an extra escalation letter that went beyond the initial scope of our agreement. I also mailed a letter directly to the corporate address, which was similarly outside the original scope. Therefore, if you agree, I would like to send the invoice together with the approximately \$70 in out-of-pocket expenses directly through Zelle or Venmo, then close the Upwork contract for payment so that we can cleanly conclude this stage.

After that is resolved, we can proceed with whichever enforcement route you select. Best [FREELANCER_NAME_001]
